chunks: Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ‘Alā ibn Razīn, from Shu’ayb Al-‘Aqraqūfi, from Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'What is the reward and recompense for the one who visits the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him)? May I be your ransom.' He replied, 'O Shu’ayb! No one establishes prayer next to him without Allāh accepting it, and no one supplicates next to him without his supplication being answered, either immediately or eventually.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, tell me more about it.' He replied, 'O Shu’ayb! The least (rewarding statement) with which a visitor of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him) will be addressed is: 'O Slave of Allāh! Verily your sins have been forgiven.' Therefore, start again with new deeds.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and benefits of visiting the grave of Imam al-Husain (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Ṣādiq (a.s.) highlights the grave of Imām al-Ḥusain (a.s.) as a locus of divine acceptance (*maqbul*) for obligatory prayers and a place where supplications are answered both swiftly and ultimately. The Imam’s instruction to 'start with a new deed' underscores the Shia concept of spiritual renewal (*tajdīd*), where the intercessory merit of the Imam transforms past forgiveness into a fresh beginning for future worship.
